gen-irish-grover-gf-noto-sans-multani: Irish Grover has tall, sturdy lowercase that makes every word look big and a little bumpy, with open throats on its a, c, e and s. Noto Sans Multani takes over where quiet matters, a plain sans with a lofty x-height.
gen-irish-grover-gf-noto-sans-myanmar: Noto Sans Myanmar lays down a thick, heavy-looking strip of text, its c opening broad and welcoming. Irish Grover brings the fun, soft and organic, and that mix is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-irish-grover-gf-noto-sans-nabataean: Noto Sans Nabataean reads with lowercase standing almost cap-tall. Irish Grover adds a gentle thick-thin rhythm in its fun, organic shapes, while the sans below keeps its s curves wide open and steady.
gen-irish-grover-gf-noto-sans-nag-mundar: Noto Sans Nag Mundari looks half unwrapped in its c and s shapes, with lowercase that nearly rivals the capitals. Irish Grover's restrained thick-thin rhythm gives the pair a playful edge.
gen-irish-grover-gf-noto-sans-nandinagar: Softly varied stroke thickness is what sets Irish Grover apart, giving its tall lowercase a sturdy, friendly look. Noto Sans Nandinagari does the opposite job, with short ascenders, a big lowercase body and generous openings at every weight.
gen-irish-grover-gf-noto-sans-newa: Noto Sans Newa has a clearly open mouth on its lowercase e. Its tall counters and bowls make a long passage feel easy to follow, while Irish Grover adds a subtle thick and thin cadence above.
gen-irish-grover-gf-noto-sans-nushu: Noto Sans Nushu holds its terminals far from the stroke body, under a towering x-height that feels modern. If Irish Grover shrinks, its sturdy fun gets lost.
gen-irish-grover-gf-noto-sans-ogham: Tall, bold-looking lowercase runs through both fonts, and Irish Grover adds slightly thinner curves at the tops of its rounded letters. Noto Sans Ogham, a plain sans with wide gaps in the e, is happiest when sized generously.
gen-irish-grover-gf-noto-sans-ol-chiki: Irish Grover has a fun, organic feel, with a slight pinch where its curves meet straight stems. And Noto Sans Ol Chiki holds its curve tails well back, so words read as solid blocks rather than skylines.
gen-irish-grover-gf-noto-sans-old-hungar: Noto Sans Old Hungarian reads with large open counters in its tall a, e and s, approachable and contemporary. And Irish Grover sits above with curves that thin out modestly where they turn, fun and organic.
